standard_prerequisites.name: Tautological instance
standard_prerequisites.statement: A tautological instance is a sentence obtained from a propositional tautology by uniformly substituting modal sentences D_1, ..., D_n for the propositional variables p_1, ..., p_n.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the class of sentences the counted proposition claims valid (1364-1366).

standard_prerequisites.name: Tautologies under valuations
standard_prerequisites.statement: A propositional tautology is true under every valuation; the unit proves this as its own lemma.
standard_prerequisites.use: It delivers the contradiction once the mimicking valuation is defined (1374-1377).

core_obligations: Contrapositive setup: assume a model M and world w where the instance A with substitutions D_i for p_i is false (1368-1371).
Define a propositional valuation v by v(p_i) = true exactly when M satisfies D_i at w, with arbitrary values elsewhere (1371-1374).
By the tautology lemma, the propositional tautology underlying A is false under v, so A is not a tautology, contradicting the assumption that A was an instance of one (1374-1377).

proof_roadmap.step: Take a countermodel world for the instance.
Define the valuation mimicking the substituted sentences.
Apply the tautology lemma to finish the contrapositive.

difficulty_reason: The counted proposition is the author proposition at source lines 1364-1366: every tautological instance of a propositional tautology, with sentence variables replaced by modal sentences, is valid at every world of every model. The author proof (1368-1377) runs the contrapositive: from a counterexample at a world it defines a propositional valuation recording the truth values of the substituted sentences at that world, invokes the unit's lemma that tautologies hold under every valuation, and concludes the substituted sentence itself is not a tautology. The construction of the mimicking valuation is the counted content.
